passage:
Bhupen: 214 people liked my winning-pitch post!! 🎉
Alka: Congrats, you deserved it.
Bhupen: Honestly the other teams weren't even close. I think I just see things others don't.
Alka: 😅 Bhupen.
Bhupen: What? It's true. Everyone keeps saying I'm a natural.
Alka: Wasn't it Mrs Sen's feedback that fixed your first slide? And Tarun stayed up building the demo?
Bhupen: ...yeah. And the judge did say the pricing section was weak.
Alka: Want me to tear that section apart over coffee?
Bhupen: Ugh. Yes. Sunday?
Alka: Sunday. You're buying. 😊

qa.q: How many people liked Bhupen's winning-pitch post?
What is Bhupen thinking when Bhupen says the other teams weren't even close?
qa.a: Bhupen feels superior and believes winning comes from seeing what others don't, a belief fed by constant praise.

qa.q: What could Bhupen do to keep ego from hardening?
qa.a: Take up Alka's offer to critique the pricing section, credit Mrs Sen and Tarun, and stay curious about what the judge called weak.

qa.q: How might Alka see Bhupen's win?
qa.a: Alka is happy for Bhupen, but the teasing and the questions suggest Alka worries the praise is going to Bhupen's head and offers a gentle challenge.

grounding: After a big win Bhupen feels superior; Alka reminds Bhupen of the people who helped, and Bhupen becomes willing to hear criticism.

passage:
"Hansa, you've won the state chess title, well done. Now sit, and let me tell you about my biggest mistake.

When I, Bhupen, was twenty-four, I won the national quiz championship. My picture was in the paper. Everyone in Guwahati knew my name. For a year, every person I met told me I was brilliant.

And I believed them. I stopped studying properly. When my old coach pointed out that I'd been lucky in the final round, I laughed at him. I thought critics were just jealous.

The next year I lost in the first round to a seventeen-year-old from Silchar. I sat in the hall, humiliated.

Afterwards, I went to my coach and apologised. I thanked him for all those evenings he spent with me, unpaid. I asked him to show me what I'd got wrong.

Enjoy your win, beta. Then thank your teachers, and keep listening to the ones who tell you where you slipped."

qa.q: What title did Bhupen win at twenty-four?
What was Bhupen feeling in the year after the win?
qa.a: Bhupen felt proud and superior, believing the praise and dismissing critics as jealous.

qa.q: Which turning point in Bhupen's story changed things?
qa.a: Losing in the first round and then going back to the coach to apologise, thank him and ask what went wrong.

qa.q: How might the old coach have seen Bhupen's laugh after the win?
qa.a: The coach may have felt hurt and worried, seeing Bhupen's ego block any listening.

grounding: An elder recalls feeling superior after a big win, dismissing critics, and learning to remember the coach's support and keep listening.

passage:
Vikas had four hours before the investors' dinner in Kochi, and his startup had just won the national innovation prize. His phone buzzed nonstop with congratulations. Strangers called him a genius.

He liked it. A lot. On the auto ride to the hotel, he practised how he'd tell the story: his idea, his vision.

Then Jomon, his co-founder, texted: "Great speech. Did you mention Ms. Mathew?"

Vikas stopped. Ms. Mathew, his college professor, had given them lab space for free for a year. He hadn't mentioned her. He hadn't mentioned the three interns either, or the lucky timing of the government scheme.

At the dinner, an older investor gently criticised their pricing model. Vikas's first instinct was to defend it.

He caught himself. "Tell me more. What are we missing?"

The investor talked for twenty minutes. Vikas took notes.

Before dessert, he stood up and thanked Ms. Mathew, the interns and Jomon by name.

qa.q: How long did Vikas have before the investors' dinner?
What was Vikas feeling during the auto ride to the hotel?
qa.a: He felt proud and pleased with the praise, enjoying being called a genius.

qa.q: What did Vikas do at the dinner that showed humility?
qa.a: He listened to the investor's criticism with curiosity instead of defending, and thanked Ms. Mathew, the interns and Jomon by name.

qa.q: How might Jomon feel when Vikas thanks him publicly?
qa.a: Jomon would likely feel appreciated and glad that Vikas remembered everyone who helped 🙂.

grounding: Under the pressure of an investors' dinner, the passage shows someone enjoying a big win and praise, then remembering the support behind it and choosing to listen to critics.
